jobs.title: Vice President, Revenue Operations and Commercial Excellence
jobs.description:
What we will offer you:

Culture:
Join a supportive and inclusive work environment where teamwork, respect, and open communication are at the core of everything we do.
Opportunity:
A continuous focus on professional development with many opportunities for training & career growth.
Health & Wellness:
Competitive health benefits right from the start including health & wellness spending accounts & maternity leave top-up. Access our employee assistance program for confidential counseling, mental health support, and various resources to help you navigate life’s challenges.
Competitive Compensation:
We offer a highly competitive salary package, ensuring that your hard work and dedication are recognized and rewarded accordingly.
Flexibility:
We understand the importance of work-life balance, we offer flexible hybrid work options to help you manage your personal and professional commitments.
Technology:
Work with state-of-the-art tools and technologies that empower you to excel in your role and stay at the forefront of industry trends.
Safety Focused:
We care about you and have committed to a zero-harm workplace.

Build the commercial engine that powers profitable growth.

Reporting to the Chief Commercial Officer, the Vice-President, Revenue Operations & Commercial Excellence is a transformational executive leader responsible for building the capabilities, insights, governance and operating disciplines that enable predictable, profitable growth across the organization. As a key strategic partner to the executive team, you will connect commercial strategy, planning, pricing, analytics, technology and execution across the customer lifecycle, creating a unified view of performance that enables smarter decisions and stronger business outcomes across North America.

This role is ideal for a strategic and commercially minded leader who excels at translating complexity into action. You bring a balance of analytical rigor, operational excellence and change leadership, along with the ability to influence across functions, build high-performing teams and drive enterprise-wide alignment. Leveraging data, customer insights and business performance indicators, you will help shape the commercial capabilities, processes and ways of working that accelerate growth, improve productivity and strengthen profitability.

What You'll Do:

Lead enterprise-wide commercial planning, forecasting and performance management processes, ensuring alignment between growth objectives, resource priorities and financial outcomes.
Build and maintain a consolidated view of commercial performance, customer trends, risks and opportunities to enable timely, data-driven decision-making.
Develop executive scorecards, operating reviews and performance reporting that provide visibility into growth, retention, productivity and profitability.
Lead scenario planning and commercial modelling activities to support strategic investments, resource allocation decisions and growth initiatives.
Establish pricing strategies, governance frameworks and decision guardrails that strengthen price realization, improve margin performance and support sustainable growth.
Partner closely with Commercial, Finance and Operations leaders to improve forecasting accuracy, demand visibility and business planning effectiveness.
Advance commercial analytics and business intelligence capabilities by partnering with Data & Analytics and IT to strengthen reporting, governance and decision support.
Champion predictive analytics, automation and AI-enabled solutions that improve productivity, enhance data quality and accelerate decision-making.
Shape the commercial technology roadmap, ensuring CRM, analytics and other commercial platforms are integrated, scalable and aligned to business needs.
Establish common commercial processes, governance structures and operating rhythms that improve consistency, accountability and execution across functions.
Strengthen sales effectiveness through CRM governance, pipeline management, territory design, quota planning, incentive administration and forecasting disciplines.
Lead the development of enablement strategies, tools, training programs and playbooks that build organizational capability and support commercial excellence.
Build, develop and lead a multidisciplinary team spanning revenue operations, pricing, analytics, sales operations, performance management and commercial enablement.
Allocate resources and specialized capabilities against the organization's highest-value commercial priorities and growth opportunities.
Serve as a trusted advisor to the Chief Commercial Officer and Commercial Leadership Team, bringing insights, recommendations and constructive challenge to key business decisions.
Lead enterprise-wide transformation initiatives that improve alignment, accountability and execution across Sales, Marketing, Customer Experience, Retention, Finance, Operations, Data & Analytics, IT and Legal.

What You'll Bring:

University degree in Business, Finance, Economics, Engineering or a related field. MBA or relevant professional designation is an asset.
10+ years of executive leadership experience in Revenue Operations, Commercial Excellence, Commercial Strategy, Sales Operations, FP&A, Pricing, Analytics or related disciplines.
Demonstrated success building or transforming enterprise-scale commercial capabilities across complex organizations.
Strong experience in commercial planning, forecasting, pricing, analytics and performance management.
Proven ability to influence senior stakeholders, lead through change and drive alignment across functions.
Experience operating across Canada and the United States is an asset.
Fluency in English required to support our North American business.
Ability to travel across Canada and the United States.
Legal authorization to work in the United States or Canada is required. We will not sponsor employment visas now or in the future for this role.

Why Join Us?

This is a rare opportunity to build and lead the commercial capabilities that will shape our future growth. You'll partner closely with executive leadership to influence strategy, strengthen performance and create the systems, insights and ways of working that drive long-term success across North America.

Work Location:
Preference is for candidates located within commuting distance of Calgary, AB; Greater Toronto, ON; Wayne, PA; or Rochester, NY. However, remote candidates will be considered for the right fit.

This posting is a replacement for an existing vacancy. We do not use AI tools in the selection process and do not request pay history.

jobs.title: Director of Finance
jobs.description:
Are you looking for a role where you can roll up your sleeves and make a difference? Our manufacturing industry client outside the Ottawa area is currently recruiting a Director of Finance. The Director of Finance leads the financial planning and performance agenda. As a member of the leadership team, you will advise on profitability, investment and long-term priorities. You will bring clear financial judgment to business decisions and help build a team that supports strong financial and operational results.

Reporting to the CFO, the Director of Finance is responsible for:

Operating costs and profitability

Lead the financial view of plant costs, capacity and product profitability.
Partner with plant leadership to achieve cost-per-unit targets.
Oversee product cost models and guide action on performance gaps.
Guide costing methods with Finance, within approved accounting policies.
Partner with plant leaders to strengthen the reliability of costing inputs.
Provide financial oversight of inventory performance, working capital and related risks.

Planning and performance

Lead budgets, forecasts and capital planning in line with long-term priorities.
Partner with leaders to translate long-range site and operating plans into a sound financial plan.
Set a consistent planning approach with clear assumptions and ownership.
Lead financial reviews focused on results, risks and decisions.
Deliver clear reporting and outlooks to leadership, and the Board as needed.
Ensure planning and analysis draw on reliable, consistent financial information.

Business decisions and improvement

Advise plant leadership on operating choices, investment priorities and financial risk.
Guide capital evaluation and investment reviews.
Set financial targets with leaders and drive sustainable cost improvements.
Shape better use of financial systems and reporting tools to improve insight and efficiency.
Partner with process owners on finance improvements, making the most of existing systems.
Strengthen data ownership, process discipline and continuity.

Leadership and financial stewardship

Build strong partnerships and shared financial ownership across the organization.
Lead planning and analysis while respecting established accounting and transaction responsibilities.
Uphold financial controls, company policies and site safety, environmental and quality standards.
Promote open and honest communication.
Fosters "team building" and a culture focused on problem solving / process improvement.
Carry out other related duties as required.

Requirements

Undergraduate degree in finance, accounting or economics; CPA preferred.
8+ years in operations finance within manufacturing industry.
Strong understanding of manufacturing costs, forecasting, financial modelling and capital evaluation.
Clear, collaborative communication style.
Sound business judgment and the ability to turn financial insight into clear decisions.
A practical approach to process and data improvement; large ERP experience preferred.

Additional Information:

The Mason Group is committed to fostering a diverse, inclusive, and accessible recruitment process. We welcome applicants from all qualified candidates. Accommodations are available upon request for candidates participating in all stages of the recruitment process, in accordance with the Accessibility for Ontarians with Disabilities Act (AODA).

This role is for an immediate vacancy, and we are actively hiring.

Technology-assisted screening tools including AI may be used during the recruitment process; however, all applications are reviewed by our Consultants.

If you are already registered with The Mason Group, please contact your Recruiting Consultant directly with reference to job #21580.

jobs.title: Commercial Finance Director
jobs.description:
Summary

Are you a high-energy finance leader with a talent for navigating complex commercial landscapes and driving strategic growth?

We are seeking a Commercial Finance Director to provide pivotal commercial support for a high-growth portfolio within our Connectivity & Cloud Solutions (CCS) segment. This portfolio of accounts is projected to increase significantly in 2027 and beyond, and this role is critical to managing the financial and operational success of new and existing large customers. In this hyper-growth environment, you will have the unique opportunity to shape the financial trajectory of our fastest-scaling accounts.

You will act as a key business partner, managing the commercial aspects as well as the full P&L for some of the largest accounts in Celestica. You will bridge the gap between finance, supply chain, engineering, and executive leadership to ensure profitable execution and strategic alignment.

Detailed Description

Performs tasks such as, but not limited to, the following:
Commercial Leadership:
Lead all commercial aspects for assigned high-growth customers, including contract management, pricing discussions, and the implementation of service elements.
Strategic Planning & Forecasting:
Drive the finalization of the Annual Operating Plan (AOP), 3-year Strategic Plan (SP), and monthly financial forecasts for the Global Customer Business Unit (GCBU).
Executive Reporting:
Prepare and present frequent updates to the Executive Leadership Team (ELT) (monthly or bi-weekly) regarding portfolio performance, risks, and opportunities.
Cross-Functional Collaboration:
Partner with customer, sales and production teams to ensure financial readiness for new product introductions and large-scale bookings.
Financial Analysis:
Perform quantitative and qualitative analysis to support key customer negotiations and drive cash or profit improvements.
Global Coordination:
Manage financial expectations and solutions across multiple international manufacturing sites to ensure alignment on forecasts and outlooks.

Knowledge/Skills/Competencies

Strategic Business Partnering:
Proven ability to influence and negotiate effectively across cross-functional teams, including Supply Chain, Engineering, and GCBU leaders.
Commercial Acumen:
Expertise in managing complex commercial elements such as contracts, pricing strategies, and unique deal constructs.
Analytical Excellence:
Exceptional attention to detail with the ability to decipher key dynamics influencing financial results and pinpointing areas for margin enhancement.
Communication:
Skilled at communicating complex financial data and strategic outlooks to the ELT, the customer and other external stakeholders.
Adaptability:
Adept at managing multiple complex initiatives under tight deadlines within a dynamic, global environment spanning multiple international sites.

Physical Demands

Duties of this position are performed in a normal office environment
Duties may require extended periods of sitting and sustained visual concentration on a computer monitor or on numbers and other detailed data
Repetitive manual movements are frequently required (e.g. data entry, using a computer mouse, using a calculator, etc)
Occasional overnight travel is required

Typical Experience

10+ years of progressive, relevant finance experience.
Commercial finance experience is strongly preferred.

Typical Education

Bachelor’s degree in Finance or Accounting.
CPA or equivalent accounting designation is preferred.

Notes

This job description is not intended to be an exhaustive list of all duties and responsibilities of the position. Employees are held accountable for all duties of the job. Job duties and the % of time identified for any function are subject to change at any time.

Celestica is an Equal Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, pregnancy, genetic information, disability, status as a protected veteran, or any other protected category under applicable federal, state, and local laws.
At Celestica we are committed to fostering an inclusive, accessible environment, where all employees and customers feel valued, respected and supported. Special arrangements can be made for candidates who need it throughout the hiring process. Please indicate your needs and we will work with you to meet them.
COMPANY OVERVIEW:

Celestica, Inc. (NYSE: CLS; TSX: CLS) is a technology leader dedicated to driving customer success and market advancements. With deep expertise in design, engineering, manufacturing, supply chain, and platform solutions, Celestica enables critical data center infrastructure for AI, cloud, and hybrid cloud and advances technologies in high-growth markets. With a talented team and a strategic global network, Celestica helps its customers achieve competitive advantages.
Today, Celestica delivers innovative supply chain solutions globally to customers in strategic two operating and reporting segments: Advanced Technology Solutions (ATS) and Connectivity and Cloud Solutions (CC):
ATS:
This segment serves customers in complex, regulated and high-reliability markets such as Industrial & Smart Energy, Aerospace & Defense, Semiconductor Capital Equipment, and HealthTech. It is engineering led, with deep expertise in design, manufacturing and lifecycle solutions.
CCS:
This segment focuses on high-performance technology solutions and services for the data center, serving hyperscalers, digital native customers and enterprises. Celestica's Platform Solutions offering provides innovative and customizable computing, storage and networking solutions enabling AI-driven growth.
Built on a legacy of trust and performance, Celestica has earned its reputation by delivering results in complex and fast-changing markets. Celestica exceeds customer expectations by identifying trends and staying ahead of the curve. Backed by comprehensive capabilities and a global network across North America, Europe and Asia, Celestica helps customers gain competitive advantage with the quality, flexibility and resiliency they need to respond quickly to shifts in demand. Guided by a bold vision to accelerate market advancements, Celestica delivers innovative solutions and technologies that turn complexity into opportunity. Anchored in teamwork and commitment, Celestica strives to be the most trusted partner to its customers and colleagues worldwide.
We use artificial intelligence tools to assist in screening and assessing applications for this role. All hiring decisions involve human review.
This posting is for an existing vacancy.
Celestica would like to thank all applicants, however, only qualified applicants will be contacted.
Celestica does not accept unsolicited resumes from recruitment agencies or fee based recruitment services.

jobs.title: VP, Supply and Trading and Renewable Energy
jobs.description:
Job Title:
VP, Supply and Trading, Renewable Energy

Division:
Renewable Energy

Location:
Toronto (Mississauga office) or Montreal (Varennes office)

Reports To:
Executive Vice President and Co-Head, Renewable Energy

Vacancy Status:
This posting represents an active vacancy for which we are currently hiring.

Who We Are

Every day, people around the world take medicine, pour a drink, wash their hands, wear a fragrance, or fill up their car. Most of them never think about what’s inside. We do, because a lot of it starts with us.

Greenfield Global produces the high-purity alcohols, specialty solvents, custom blends, bioprocessing inputs, and low-carbon fuels that industries in more than 50 countries depend on. Founded in 1989 as a single plant in Tiverton, Ontario, we now operate ethanol distilleries in Ontario and Québec, manufacturing and packaging facilities in Canada, the United States, and Ireland, and a globally integrated supply chain. Because we’re the producer and not a middleman, we control every step from sourcing and testing to delivery, giving customers exceptional quality, reliability, and support.

About The Role

The Vice President (VP), Supply and Trading leads the commercial supply and trading activities of the Renewable Energy business unit, with a focus on renewable fuels and related environmental markets. The VP is responsible for product supply, physical trading, environmental credits and market risk management, with a mandate to optimize margins across ethanol and other renewable fuel products while developing the commercial capabilities required to support the growth of new low-carbon solutions.

What You’ll Do

Build, lead, and develop a high-performing supply and trading team.
Manage ethanol supply, sales and distribution relationships with refiners, marketers, and terminals, including the negotiation and management of commercial contracts, terms and conditions.
Trade and optimize environmental attributes, including Clean Fuel Regulations (CFR) credits, Low Carbon Fuel Standard (LCFS) credits, Renewable Identification Numbers (RINs), the Quebec SPEDE/Cap & Trade credits and European certificates.
Approve feedstock and co-product strategies on behalf of Renewable Energy.
Lead logistics strategy of the Renewable Energy supply network.
Develop and maintain hedging strategies and risk policies in partnership with Finance and Risk.
Support offtake strategy and commercial structuring for new products, including e-methanol and other low-carbon molecules.
Track and interpret policy and market developments (CFR, LCFS, the European Renewable Energy Directive, and provincial mandates) and translate them into commercial positioning.
Provide market intelligence, forecasts, and performance reporting to Renewable Energy executive leadership.
Oversee market intelligence activities and manage subscriptions to market data and pricing services to support commercial decision-making.
Lead supply strategies for the purchase and resale of products, identifying market opportunities and optimizing value across the portfolio.

About You

At least 12 years in energy, biofuels, or commodity trading, including at least five in a senior leadership role.
Deep knowledge of ethanol and low-carbon fuel markets and environmental credit programs.
Proven record managing physical supply, price risk, and counterparty exposure.
Strong commercial negotiation and structuring skills; experience with long-term offtake or supply agreements is an asset.
Bachelor’s degree in business, engineering, economics, or a related field.
Functional in English and French.
Demonstrated ability to take full ownership and accountability for decisions, results, and business outcomes.
Proven ability to build strong, trusted relationships with internal and external stakeholders.
Exceptional communication skills, with the ability to communicate complex issues clearly, directly, and effectively at all levels of the organization.
Strong and decisive leadership, with the ability to set direction, make difficult decisions, and lead with conviction.
Strong executive presence and demonstrated ability to influence, engage, and mobilize others.
Strong commercial and financial acumen, with a demonstrated focus on maximizing profitability and value creation.
Ability to navigate ambiguity, complexity, and rapidly changing market conditions while maintaining sound judgment and strategic focus.
Demonstrated resilience and perseverance, with the ability to remain effective and solution-oriented in the face of challenges and adversity.
Provide leadership, coaching and mentorship to the commercial team, fostering talent development, knowledge sharing and strong succession.

What Success Looks Like

Improved margin capture and reduced volatility.
Optimize value across products, markets and jurisdictions
A scalable trading platform ready to support new low-carbon products.
Elevate the strategic and executive leadership scope of the role.

Why You’ll Love Working at Greenfield

At Greenfield, you’ll do more than build a career, you’ll be part of a team working to create sustainable solutions that make a positive impact on the world. We believe great work happens when talented people are empowered to learn, grow, collaborate, and bring their ideas to life.

When You Join Greenfield, You Can Expect

Meaningful work with the opportunity to make a real impact.
A collaborative, supportive team that values growth, innovation, and open communication.
Opportunities to learn, develop, and advance your career.
Comprehensive health and dental benefits for you and your family.
Disability coverage, life insurance, paid sick time, and other programs that support your well-being.
Vacation time that exceeds industry standards.
A company-funded retirement savings program to help you plan for the future.

We’re building a culture where people feel valued, supported, and inspired to do their best work, and we’d love for you to be part of it.

Our Hiring Approach

At Greenfield, people make hiring decisions. Every application is reviewed by our team, and we believe in taking the time to get to know the individuals behind the resumes. While we may use technology to help streamline administrative tasks, it is never used to make hiring decisions on our behalf. We are committed to a fair, transparent, and respectful hiring experience for every candidate.

Belong at Greenfield

At Greenfield, we believe our differences make us stronger. We are committed to creating an inclusive workplace where everyone feels welcomed, respected, valued, and empowered to be their authentic selves.

We welcome and encourage applications from people of all backgrounds, experiences, and perspectives. We are proud to foster a workplace where opportunities are based on skills, qualifications, and potential, and where every individual has the chance to grow, contribute, and thrive.

If you require accommodation at any stage of the recruitment process, we’re here to help and will work with you to meet your needs.

About The Salary Range

At Greenfield Global, we are committed to fair and transparent compensation practices. The salary range shared for this role is intended as a guideline and does not represent a guaranteed offer. We carefully consider the responsibilities of the position, market benchmarks, and internal equity when determining compensation. Your specific offer will reflect your experience, skills, qualifications, and the unique value you bring to the role.

jobs.title: Director, Technology Operations
jobs.description:
Director, Technical Operations (Platform)

Job Type:
Permanent Full Time

Location:
Hybrid - Toronto, Ontario

Reporting to:
Chief Technology Officer

Salary
: $160,000 – $190,000 CAD

Job Purpose

The Director, Technology Operations owns the operational health of the platforms Goway sells and services travel on: our reservations platform, the infrastructure it runs on, the supplier, air and distribution integrations it depends on, and the automation and data pipelines built around it.

This is a practice-building role. You will define and own Goway's technical operations discipline: service levels, incident management, change control, observability and operational readiness, and you will make them the standard across our technology organisation. You will work alongside other Technology leaders. You will own the technology operations of our platform. You will have the CTO's mandate and backing to build the practice.

What will be your key responsibilities?

Reliability and service management

Define, publish and report service levels and service-level objectives for revenue-critical services, starting with quoting, booking, payment and traveller servicing.
Own incident management end to end: severity definitions, escalation, incident command, communication during an incident, and post-incident review with corrective actions.
Own RCA and problem management.
Own change and release management as a company standard, balancing delivery throughput against change failure rate.
Build observability sufficient to detect degradation.
Own disaster recovery and business continuity for platform services, tested and documented on a stated cadence.

Integration and supplier platform operations

Monitoring of integration paths, error and failure-rate thresholds, and defined fallback behaviour when a partner degrades.
Maintain a dependency map of the external platforms our revenue-generating flows rely on, with assessed operational risk and mitigation for each.
Own operational readiness for new integrations and new product lines entering the platform.
Own the operational reliability of automation and data pipelines in production.

Platform and cloud operations

Day-to-day operation of the AWS and managed hosting infrastructure serving our platform estate: environments, provisioning, patching and lifecycle management.
Own hosting cost governance: visibility by service, a unit-cost measure, and an annual optimisation target.
Lead capacity planning against forecast booking and travel volumes.
Reduce manual, repeatable operational work through automation.
Address seasonal capacity planning, change freezes and enhanced coverage aligned to our booking and departure peaks and to new product launches.

Vendors, partners and compliance

Platform, hosting and integration partner relationships: SLA definition, enforcement and structured performance review.
Reduce single points of dependency, whether on a vendor or an individual.
Partner with security on vulnerability management, patch compliance, access control and audit readiness.

Practice leadership and stakeholder engagement

Build and maintain a multi-year technical operations roadmap aligned to Goway's growth plans.
Report operational performance, risk and investment needs to the CTO and executive team in business terms.

What are we looking for?

Required

8 or more years in platform operations, technical operations, infrastructure or site reliability engineering, including 5 or more years in a lead or leadership capacity.
Demonstrated accountability for the availability and performance of a revenue-critical transactional platform.
Evidence of having built operational practice where little existed: SLOs, incident management, change control and observability introduced from the ground up, with measurable improvement to show for it.
Hands-on depth in AWS, including cost management and multi-environment operation.
Substantial experience operating and governing third-party platforms and integrations, including holding vendors to service levels.
Ability to set standards and drive adoption across teams.
Ability to communicate operational risk and performance.

Preferred

Experience stabilising and operationalising new systems.
Infrastructure-as-code and container orchestration experience.
AWS Certified DevOps Engineer (Professional), or AWS Certified CloudOps Engineer (Associate). Solutions Architect certifications are welcome, but less relevant to this role than the operations-focused ones.
Bachelor's degree in computer science, information technology, engineering or equivalent practical experience.

What can you expect from Goway?

Imagine working for a company where your career feels like an adventure. At Goway, you’ll join a global community that supports one another:
We offer a competitive salary accompanied by performance incentives, and we place real importance on time away from work, such as paid personal days for when life calls for them and your birthday off each year.
Our commitment to professional growth means you’ll have access to continuous learning and industry-leading training that keeps you at the forefront of travel innovation.
You’ll enjoy generous paid time off, including [three] weeks of vacation, [six] personal days, and a dedicated day off to celebrate your birthday.
Travel is in our DNA, so you’ll enjoy exclusive perks and discounts on worldwide getaways.
Since we operate across Toronto, Vancouver, Los Angeles, Manila, Sydney, and beyond, you’ll collaborate across cultures and shape a career path that reflects your ambitions.
Goway is an equal-opportunity employer. We celebrate differences and are committed to fostering an inclusive workplace for everyone. We appreciate every applicant’s interest. Please be advised that only those selected for an interview will be contacted.

How To Apply

December 11th, 2026 at 11:59pm

ABOUT ENERQUALITY

EnerQUALITY (EQ) is a recognized leader in advancing energy efficiency, sustainability, and innovation in Canada's residential construction industry. Through certification, education, and strategic industry partnerships, we empower home builders and industry professionals to build better homes while driving market transformation. A wholly owned subsidiary of the Ontario Home Builders’ Association (OHBA), EnerQUALITY is entering an exciting new chapter focused on growth, innovation and expanding its value to the residential construction industry.

ABOUT THE ROLE

The President/CEO provides visionary leadership for EQ and is accountable to the Board of Directors for advancing the organization's mission, strategic direction, financial sustainability, operational excellence, and long-term growth. The President/CEO leads the organization through effective governance, stakeholder engagement, innovation, and organizational leadership while ensuring EQ remains a trusted leader in the better built housing segment.

PILLARS OF THE ROLE

1. Strategy & Organizational Performance

Key Responsibilities
· Develop, implement, and regularly review EnerQuality's multi-year Strategic Plan.
· Translate strategic priorities into annual business plans, budgets, and measurable objectives.
· Monitor organizational performance and ensure alignment between strategic goals, operational priorities, and available resources.
· Assess market trends, risks, and emerging opportunities to inform strategic decision-making.
· Identify organizational capabilities required to support future growth and implement plans to address capability gaps.
· Provide regular performance reporting to the Board and proactively identify risks that may impact strategic objectives.

Accountabilities
· Board-approved Strategic and Annual Business Plans.
· Successful execution of strategic priorities.
· Achievement of annual organizational and financial objectives.
· Timely reporting of organizational performance and strategic risks.
· Continuous improvement in organizational effectiveness.

2. Business Development, Innovation & Revenue Growth

Key Responsibilities
· Lead the identification, evaluation, and development of new business opportunities that advance EnerQuality's mission and financial sustainability.
· Build and maintain strategic relationships with governments, utilities, builders, developers, industry associations, financial institutions, suppliers, and other partners.
· Develop and maintain a diversified pipeline of programs, products, services, funding opportunities, sponsorships, and strategic partnerships.
· Oversee development of business cases and implementation plans for new initiatives.
· Strengthen existing client and partner relationships while expanding opportunities for collaboration and revenue growth.
· Ensure customer and stakeholder feedback informs future service offerings and business development activities.

Accountabilities
· Sustainable growth in earned revenue and funding.
· Diversified and healthy business development pipeline.
· Expansion of strategic partnerships and market opportunities.
· High customer retention and stakeholder satisfaction.
· Successful launch of new programs and services that achieve business objectives.

3. Brand Leadership & Stakeholder Relations

Key Responsibilities
· Position EnerQuality as a recognized leader in energy efficiency, sustainable housing, and program delivery.
· Establish strategic communications priorities that support organizational objectives.
· Champion EnerQuality's reputation through industry leadership, public speaking, media engagement, and participation in conferences and sector initiatives.
· Foster productive relationships with government, industry, Indigenous communities, partners, funders, customers, and other stakeholders.
· Oversee marketing and communications strategies that strengthen brand awareness and support business growth.
· Ensure consistent messaging and alignment across all organizational initiatives.

Accountabilities
· Enhanced organizational profile and credibility.
· Strong stakeholder confidence and engagement.
· Effective marketing and communications aligned with strategic priorities.
· Increased awareness of EnerQuality's programs and services.
· Recognition of EnerQuality as a trusted industry partner.

4. Operational Excellence & Organizational Leadership

Key Responsibilities
· Provide executive leadership that promotes accountability, collaboration, innovation, and high performance.
· Ensure the organization has the appropriate structure, talent, systems, and resources to achieve its strategic objectives.
· Foster an inclusive, values-driven workplace culture focused on employee engagement and continuous improvement.
· Oversee financial management, business operations, technology, and administrative functions to ensure effective and efficient organizational performance.
· Ensure appropriate business continuity, operational controls, documentation, and risk management practices are maintained.
· Lead organizational planning for new initiatives and ensure operational readiness for successful implementation.

Accountabilities
· Effective and efficient organizational operations.
· Strong financial stewardship and responsible resource management.
· Engaged, high-performing workforce.
· Compliance with internal policies and sound management practices.
· Organizational readiness to support growth and change.

5. Governance, Risk & Board Relations

Key Responsibilities
· Serve as the primary liaison between management and the Board of Directors.
· Support the Board in fulfilling its governance responsibilities through timely, accurate, and transparent reporting.
· Implement Board-approved strategic priorities and annual work plans.
· Ensure compliance with all corporate, statutory, regulatory, and contractual obligations.
· Oversee enterprise risk management and ensure appropriate mitigation strategies are in place.
· Lead preparation of the Annual Report, audited financial statements, and Annual General Meeting materials.
· Foster a culture of integrity, accountability, transparency, and ethical leadership throughout the organization.

Accountabilities
· Strong and productive relationship with the Board of Directors.
· Effective governance practices and regulatory compliance.
· Timely, accurate, and transparent reporting.
· Effective enterprise risk management.
· Continued confidence of the Board, shareholders, funders, and key stakeholders.
· Achievement of organizational objectives in accordance with EnerQuality's mission, values, and strategic priorities.

IS THIS ROLE RIGHT FOR YOU?

Strategic Thinking

Sees around corners. Connects macro trends while anticipating tactical moves the company should make six to eighteen months ahead. Sets direction with conviction while remaining adaptable

Executive Presence & Communication

Commands a room. Presents the company's story, vision, and value proposition. The organization's face and voice — compelling in every setting.

Relationship Capital & Inspiration

Inspires staff and partners not through title but through authentic energy and a compelling vision. Builds genuine, long-term relationships. Understands that trust is an asset.

Financial Acumen

Financial statement fluency – what’s healthy and what’s not. Understand key metrics for the organization. Connecting numbers to decisions. Understand risk awareness.

Political Savvy, Grounded in Reality

Navigates organizational and political dynamics with sophistication — knows when to push, when to wait, and when to find an alternative path. Never loses sight of practical outcomes.

Opportunity Identification

Wired to spot emerging trends, technologies, and policy developments that influence residential building performance. Converts market intelligence and relationship insight into profitable services, or strategic alliances.

Builder & Construction Intelligence

Speaks the vocabulary of builders and industry partners without needing a translator.

Government Fluency

Understands how decisions are made at all levels of government. Engages regulatory and legislative processes as a participant, not just a subject.

Operational Efficiency

Understands how to get the best out of people and leverage tools and processes to maximize productivity without losing sight of the human relationships that drive this industry.

HOW TO APPLY

new_jobs.title: Vice President, Revenue Operations and Commercial Excellence
new_jobs.description:
What we will offer you:

Culture:
Join a supportive and inclusive work environment where teamwork, respect, and open communication are at the core of everything we do.
Opportunity:
A continuous focus on professional development with many opportunities for training & career growth.
Health & Wellness:
Competitive health benefits right from the start including health & wellness spending accounts & maternity leave top-up. Access our employee assistance program for confidential counseling, mental health support, and various resources to help you navigate life’s challenges.
Competitive Compensation:
We offer a highly competitive salary package, ensuring that your hard work and dedication are recognized and rewarded accordingly.
Flexibility:
We understand the importance of work-life balance, we offer flexible hybrid work options to help you manage your personal and professional commitments.
Technology:
Work with state-of-the-art tools and technologies that empower you to excel in your role and stay at the forefront of industry trends.
Safety Focused:
We care about you and have committed to a zero-harm workplace.

Build the commercial engine that powers profitable growth.

Reporting to the Chief Commercial Officer, the Vice-President, Revenue Operations & Commercial Excellence is a transformational executive leader responsible for building the capabilities, insights, governance and operating disciplines that enable predictable, profitable growth across the organization. As a key strategic partner to the executive team, you will connect commercial strategy, planning, pricing, analytics, technology and execution across the customer lifecycle, creating a unified view of performance that enables smarter decisions and stronger business outcomes across North America.

This role is ideal for a strategic and commercially minded leader who excels at translating complexity into action. You bring a balance of analytical rigor, operational excellence and change leadership, along with the ability to influence across functions, build high-performing teams and drive enterprise-wide alignment. Leveraging data, customer insights and business performance indicators, you will help shape the commercial capabilities, processes and ways of working that accelerate growth, improve productivity and strengthen profitability.

What You'll Do:

Lead enterprise-wide commercial planning, forecasting and performance management processes, ensuring alignment between growth objectives, resource priorities and financial outcomes.
Build and maintain a consolidated view of commercial performance, customer trends, risks and opportunities to enable timely, data-driven decision-making.
Develop executive scorecards, operating reviews and performance reporting that provide visibility into growth, retention, productivity and profitability.
Lead scenario planning and commercial modelling activities to support strategic investments, resource allocation decisions and growth initiatives.
Establish pricing strategies, governance frameworks and decision guardrails that strengthen price realization, improve margin performance and support sustainable growth.
Partner closely with Commercial, Finance and Operations leaders to improve forecasting accuracy, demand visibility and business planning effectiveness.
Advance commercial analytics and business intelligence capabilities by partnering with Data & Analytics and IT to strengthen reporting, governance and decision support.
Champion predictive analytics, automation and AI-enabled solutions that improve productivity, enhance data quality and accelerate decision-making.
Shape the commercial technology roadmap, ensuring CRM, analytics and other commercial platforms are integrated, scalable and aligned to business needs.
Establish common commercial processes, governance structures and operating rhythms that improve consistency, accountability and execution across functions.
Strengthen sales effectiveness through CRM governance, pipeline management, territory design, quota planning, incentive administration and forecasting disciplines.
Lead the development of enablement strategies, tools, training programs and playbooks that build organizational capability and support commercial excellence.
Build, develop and lead a multidisciplinary team spanning revenue operations, pricing, analytics, sales operations, performance management and commercial enablement.
Allocate resources and specialized capabilities against the organization's highest-value commercial priorities and growth opportunities.
Serve as a trusted advisor to the Chief Commercial Officer and Commercial Leadership Team, bringing insights, recommendations and constructive challenge to key business decisions.
Lead enterprise-wide transformation initiatives that improve alignment, accountability and execution across Sales, Marketing, Customer Experience, Retention, Finance, Operations, Data & Analytics, IT and Legal.

What You'll Bring:

University degree in Business, Finance, Economics, Engineering or a related field. MBA or relevant professional designation is an asset.
10+ years of executive leadership experience in Revenue Operations, Commercial Excellence, Commercial Strategy, Sales Operations, FP&A, Pricing, Analytics or related disciplines.
Demonstrated success building or transforming enterprise-scale commercial capabilities across complex organizations.
Strong experience in commercial planning, forecasting, pricing, analytics and performance management.
Proven ability to influence senior stakeholders, lead through change and drive alignment across functions.
Experience operating across Canada and the United States is an asset.
Fluency in English required to support our North American business.
Ability to travel across Canada and the United States.
Legal authorization to work in the United States or Canada is required. We will not sponsor employment visas now or in the future for this role.

Why Join Us?

This is a rare opportunity to build and lead the commercial capabilities that will shape our future growth. You'll partner closely with executive leadership to influence strategy, strengthen performance and create the systems, insights and ways of working that drive long-term success across North America.

Work Location:
Preference is for candidates located within commuting distance of Calgary, AB; Greater Toronto, ON; Wayne, PA; or Rochester, NY. However, remote candidates will be considered for the right fit.

This posting is a replacement for an existing vacancy. We do not use AI tools in the selection process and do not request pay history.

new_jobs.title: VP, Supply and Trading and Renewable Energy
new_jobs.description:
Job Title:
VP, Supply and Trading, Renewable Energy

Division:
Renewable Energy

Location:
Toronto (Mississauga office) or Montreal (Varennes office)

Reports To:
Executive Vice President and Co-Head, Renewable Energy

Vacancy Status:
This posting represents an active vacancy for which we are currently hiring.

Who We Are

Every day, people around the world take medicine, pour a drink, wash their hands, wear a fragrance, or fill up their car. Most of them never think about what’s inside. We do, because a lot of it starts with us.

Greenfield Global produces the high-purity alcohols, specialty solvents, custom blends, bioprocessing inputs, and low-carbon fuels that industries in more than 50 countries depend on. Founded in 1989 as a single plant in Tiverton, Ontario, we now operate ethanol distilleries in Ontario and Québec, manufacturing and packaging facilities in Canada, the United States, and Ireland, and a globally integrated supply chain. Because we’re the producer and not a middleman, we control every step from sourcing and testing to delivery, giving customers exceptional quality, reliability, and support.

About The Role

The Vice President (VP), Supply and Trading leads the commercial supply and trading activities of the Renewable Energy business unit, with a focus on renewable fuels and related environmental markets. The VP is responsible for product supply, physical trading, environmental credits and market risk management, with a mandate to optimize margins across ethanol and other renewable fuel products while developing the commercial capabilities required to support the growth of new low-carbon solutions.

What You’ll Do

Build, lead, and develop a high-performing supply and trading team.
Manage ethanol supply, sales and distribution relationships with refiners, marketers, and terminals, including the negotiation and management of commercial contracts, terms and conditions.
Trade and optimize environmental attributes, including Clean Fuel Regulations (CFR) credits, Low Carbon Fuel Standard (LCFS) credits, Renewable Identification Numbers (RINs), the Quebec SPEDE/Cap & Trade credits and European certificates.
Approve feedstock and co-product strategies on behalf of Renewable Energy.
Lead logistics strategy of the Renewable Energy supply network.
Develop and maintain hedging strategies and risk policies in partnership with Finance and Risk.
Support offtake strategy and commercial structuring for new products, including e-methanol and other low-carbon molecules.
Track and interpret policy and market developments (CFR, LCFS, the European Renewable Energy Directive, and provincial mandates) and translate them into commercial positioning.
Provide market intelligence, forecasts, and performance reporting to Renewable Energy executive leadership.
Oversee market intelligence activities and manage subscriptions to market data and pricing services to support commercial decision-making.
Lead supply strategies for the purchase and resale of products, identifying market opportunities and optimizing value across the portfolio.

About You

At least 12 years in energy, biofuels, or commodity trading, including at least five in a senior leadership role.
Deep knowledge of ethanol and low-carbon fuel markets and environmental credit programs.
Proven record managing physical supply, price risk, and counterparty exposure.
Strong commercial negotiation and structuring skills; experience with long-term offtake or supply agreements is an asset.
Bachelor’s degree in business, engineering, economics, or a related field.
Functional in English and French.
Demonstrated ability to take full ownership and accountability for decisions, results, and business outcomes.
Proven ability to build strong, trusted relationships with internal and external stakeholders.
Exceptional communication skills, with the ability to communicate complex issues clearly, directly, and effectively at all levels of the organization.
Strong and decisive leadership, with the ability to set direction, make difficult decisions, and lead with conviction.
Strong executive presence and demonstrated ability to influence, engage, and mobilize others.
Strong commercial and financial acumen, with a demonstrated focus on maximizing profitability and value creation.
Ability to navigate ambiguity, complexity, and rapidly changing market conditions while maintaining sound judgment and strategic focus.
Demonstrated resilience and perseverance, with the ability to remain effective and solution-oriented in the face of challenges and adversity.
Provide leadership, coaching and mentorship to the commercial team, fostering talent development, knowledge sharing and strong succession.

What Success Looks Like

Improved margin capture and reduced volatility.
Optimize value across products, markets and jurisdictions
A scalable trading platform ready to support new low-carbon products.
Elevate the strategic and executive leadership scope of the role.

Why You’ll Love Working at Greenfield

At Greenfield, you’ll do more than build a career, you’ll be part of a team working to create sustainable solutions that make a positive impact on the world. We believe great work happens when talented people are empowered to learn, grow, collaborate, and bring their ideas to life.

When You Join Greenfield, You Can Expect

Meaningful work with the opportunity to make a real impact.
A collaborative, supportive team that values growth, innovation, and open communication.
Opportunities to learn, develop, and advance your career.
Comprehensive health and dental benefits for you and your family.
Disability coverage, life insurance, paid sick time, and other programs that support your well-being.
Vacation time that exceeds industry standards.
A company-funded retirement savings program to help you plan for the future.

We’re building a culture where people feel valued, supported, and inspired to do their best work, and we’d love for you to be part of it.

Our Hiring Approach

At Greenfield, people make hiring decisions. Every application is reviewed by our team, and we believe in taking the time to get to know the individuals behind the resumes. While we may use technology to help streamline administrative tasks, it is never used to make hiring decisions on our behalf. We are committed to a fair, transparent, and respectful hiring experience for every candidate.

Belong at Greenfield

At Greenfield, we believe our differences make us stronger. We are committed to creating an inclusive workplace where everyone feels welcomed, respected, valued, and empowered to be their authentic selves.

We welcome and encourage applications from people of all backgrounds, experiences, and perspectives. We are proud to foster a workplace where opportunities are based on skills, qualifications, and potential, and where every individual has the chance to grow, contribute, and thrive.

If you require accommodation at any stage of the recruitment process, we’re here to help and will work with you to meet your needs.

About The Salary Range

At Greenfield Global, we are committed to fair and transparent compensation practices. The salary range shared for this role is intended as a guideline and does not represent a guaranteed offer. We carefully consider the responsibilities of the position, market benchmarks, and internal equity when determining compensation. Your specific offer will reflect your experience, skills, qualifications, and the unique value you bring to the role.

new_jobs.title: Director, Technology Operations
new_jobs.description:
Director, Technical Operations (Platform)

Job Type:
Permanent Full Time

Location:
Hybrid - Toronto, Ontario

Reporting to:
Chief Technology Officer

Salary
: $160,000 – $190,000 CAD

Job Purpose

The Director, Technology Operations owns the operational health of the platforms Goway sells and services travel on: our reservations platform, the infrastructure it runs on, the supplier, air and distribution integrations it depends on, and the automation and data pipelines built around it.

This is a practice-building role. You will define and own Goway's technical operations discipline: service levels, incident management, change control, observability and operational readiness, and you will make them the standard across our technology organisation. You will work alongside other Technology leaders. You will own the technology operations of our platform. You will have the CTO's mandate and backing to build the practice.

What will be your key responsibilities?

Reliability and service management

Define, publish and report service levels and service-level objectives for revenue-critical services, starting with quoting, booking, payment and traveller servicing.
Own incident management end to end: severity definitions, escalation, incident command, communication during an incident, and post-incident review with corrective actions.
Own RCA and problem management.
Own change and release management as a company standard, balancing delivery throughput against change failure rate.
Build observability sufficient to detect degradation.
Own disaster recovery and business continuity for platform services, tested and documented on a stated cadence.

Integration and supplier platform operations

Monitoring of integration paths, error and failure-rate thresholds, and defined fallback behaviour when a partner degrades.
Maintain a dependency map of the external platforms our revenue-generating flows rely on, with assessed operational risk and mitigation for each.
Own operational readiness for new integrations and new product lines entering the platform.
Own the operational reliability of automation and data pipelines in production.

Platform and cloud operations

Day-to-day operation of the AWS and managed hosting infrastructure serving our platform estate: environments, provisioning, patching and lifecycle management.
Own hosting cost governance: visibility by service, a unit-cost measure, and an annual optimisation target.
Lead capacity planning against forecast booking and travel volumes.
Reduce manual, repeatable operational work through automation.
Address seasonal capacity planning, change freezes and enhanced coverage aligned to our booking and departure peaks and to new product launches.

Vendors, partners and compliance

Platform, hosting and integration partner relationships: SLA definition, enforcement and structured performance review.
Reduce single points of dependency, whether on a vendor or an individual.
Partner with security on vulnerability management, patch compliance, access control and audit readiness.

Practice leadership and stakeholder engagement

Build and maintain a multi-year technical operations roadmap aligned to Goway's growth plans.
Report operational performance, risk and investment needs to the CTO and executive team in business terms.

What are we looking for?

Required

8 or more years in platform operations, technical operations, infrastructure or site reliability engineering, including 5 or more years in a lead or leadership capacity.
Demonstrated accountability for the availability and performance of a revenue-critical transactional platform.
Evidence of having built operational practice where little existed: SLOs, incident management, change control and observability introduced from the ground up, with measurable improvement to show for it.
Hands-on depth in AWS, including cost management and multi-environment operation.
Substantial experience operating and governing third-party platforms and integrations, including holding vendors to service levels.
Ability to set standards and drive adoption across teams.
Ability to communicate operational risk and performance.

Preferred

Experience stabilising and operationalising new systems.
Infrastructure-as-code and container orchestration experience.
AWS Certified DevOps Engineer (Professional), or AWS Certified CloudOps Engineer (Associate). Solutions Architect certifications are welcome, but less relevant to this role than the operations-focused ones.
Bachelor's degree in computer science, information technology, engineering or equivalent practical experience.

What can you expect from Goway?

Imagine working for a company where your career feels like an adventure. At Goway, you’ll join a global community that supports one another:
We offer a competitive salary accompanied by performance incentives, and we place real importance on time away from work, such as paid personal days for when life calls for them and your birthday off each year.
Our commitment to professional growth means you’ll have access to continuous learning and industry-leading training that keeps you at the forefront of travel innovation.
You’ll enjoy generous paid time off, including [three] weeks of vacation, [six] personal days, and a dedicated day off to celebrate your birthday.
Travel is in our DNA, so you’ll enjoy exclusive perks and discounts on worldwide getaways.
Since we operate across Toronto, Vancouver, Los Angeles, Manila, Sydney, and beyond, you’ll collaborate across cultures and shape a career path that reflects your ambitions.
Goway is an equal-opportunity employer. We celebrate differences and are committed to fostering an inclusive workplace for everyone. We appreciate every applicant’s interest. Please be advised that only those selected for an interview will be contacted.

How To Apply
